gull.notes: Single gulls (OpenGameArt) and one NPS western-gull flock clip.

creak.notes: Wooden groans/creaks for the hull; play slowed (playbackRate 0.6-0.9) for a heavier ship.

canvas.notes: Cloth snaps/rustles for setting or furling sail.

rope.notes: Short wooden creaks standing in for rope through a block.

harbour_bell.notes: Distant church bell tolling (with birdsong); loopable bed with faded ends.

harbour_crowd.notes: Outdoor wharf with voices, faded ends; play low and low-passed for distance. (An indoor restaurant bed was dropped: it may carry background music the recordist could not license.)

thunder.notes: One sharp clap and one long rolling peal.

splash_small.notes: Small splashes / plops (fish, thrown object); about 0.5-0.8s.

splash_big.notes: Bigger splashes (~1.1-1.3s) for a dolphin re-entering or a diving bird; pitch down (playbackRate 0.7-0.85) for more weight.

dolphin.notes: Dolphin whistle chatter recorded underwater (with hydrophone hiss); low-pass for an above-water feel.

whale_song.notes: Distant humpback song for calm nights; hydrophone recordings, faded ends.

whale_blow.notes: A humpback exhaling (wheeze blow), heard through a hydrophone; low-pass and add air noise for a spout at the surface.

cannon_close.notes: A single close gun: a real salute field piece, a naval gun with reverb, a firework mortar bang; play pitched 0.85-1.1 (cannon_close_3 at 0.6-0.8) for variety.

cannon_far.notes: Distant booms (fireworks heard across open country); play low, low-passed and pitched 0.6-0.9 for an enemy broadside over the water.

ball_whistle.notes: A cannonball going over: synthesised (ball-whistle.py), a falling howl of air; play at rate 0.9-1.1.

wood_hit.notes: Short wood breaks for a ball striking the hull; play pitched 0.55-0.8 for a heavy hull, layered with a cannon_far thump.

sail_tear.notes: Heavy canvas tearing where a ball goes through the rigging: synthesised (battle-synth.py); play at rate 0.9-1.1.

mast_crack.notes: Timber cracking and falling for a mast going over; play pitched 0.6-0.8 for weight.

musket.notes: Black-powder shots and a ragged rifle volley for swivels and boarders; play pitched 0.9-1.1 and stagger singles for a volley.

melee.notes: Blades clashing in a boarding fight (sword clashes laid in a sequence); a musket volley plays with it. (Two crowd beds were dropped: earshot heard them as a crowd cheering.)

cheer.notes: Crew cheering on victory: clapping and "woo" from a small group, plus one "hurray"; play pitched 0.85-0.95 for rougher, deeper voices.

explosion.notes: Big blasts for a powder magazine: a single explosion, a sharp blast and a rolling chain; play pitched 0.5-0.7 for size.
